articles.title: Ebola disease outbreak in Congo tops 10,000 confirmed cases
articles.description: Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak has topped 10,000 confirmed cases as authorities race to slow the spread across Africa. Data from Congo's Ministry of Health on Tuesday showed there have been a total of 10,060 confirmed cases, nearly half of whom have died. It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and was declared in May. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation. It has spread farther across Africa than any previous Ebola outbreak, reaching three regions with cases recorded in Kenya and Nigeria as well.

articles.title: Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on arrivals from Congo to block Ebola spread
articles.description: Uganda has mandated a 21-day quarantine for its citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo, a measure announced by Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi to tighten Ebola precautions. The decision comes despite Uganda officially declaring its latest Ebola outbreak over in July, and follows recent positive tests among travelers who passed through the country. The quarantine requirement applies specifically to Ugandan nationals who have recently traveled to the DRC, the region where the current outbreak is active. Health officials state that all travelers entering Uganda by air, land, or water must now complete a passenger locator form, while screening at Entebbe International Airport and land border crossings has been intensified. This escalation is driven by two recent cases that raised concerns about transmission routes. In Kenya, a patient who traveled from the Congo through Uganda to Nairobi died two days after arrival. In Nigeria, a 42-year-old woman, identified as the wife of a Swiss diplomat, tested positive after returning from Uganda via Addis Ababa to Abuja on October 3. Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control reported that she is in isolation and has improved remarkably, with 53 contacts traced.
